metadata.title: Harmonic Interpolation and a Brunn-Minkowski Theorem for Random Determinants

nodes.name: Minkowski sum
nodes.statement: For convex subsets $A,B \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the Minkowski sum is $A+B := \{a+b : a \in A, b \in B\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Pointwise sum of two convex sets in Euclidean space.

nodes.name: Brunn-Minkowski inequality
nodes.statement: For convex sets $A,B \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$: $|A+B|^{1/n} \geq |A|^{1/n} + |B|^{1/n}$, where $|\cdot|$ denotes Euclidean volume.

nodes.name: Convex interpolation
nodes.statement: Given a continuous family $\{A_\tau\}_{\tau \in \partial\Omega}$ of convex bodies and convex $\Omega$, the convex interpolation is $A := \operatorname{Convexhull}\left(\bigcup_{\tau \in \partial\Omega} A_\tau \times \{\tau\}\right) \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{n+m}$, with $A_x$ the fiber over $x \in \Omega$.

nodes.name: Support function
nodes.statement: The support function of a convex set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is $h_A(\xi) := \sup_{\zeta \in A}(\zeta \cdot \xi)$; $h_A$ is convex and positively homogeneous: $h_A(t\xi) = |t| h_A(\xi)$ for $t \in \mathbb{R}$.

nodes.name: Support function properties
nodes.statement: $h_A$ is convex and $h_A(t\xi) = |t| h_A(\xi)$ for $t \in \mathbb{R}$.

nodes.name: Minkowski integral
nodes.statement: For a measure $d\mu$ on a measurable set $D \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ and a family of convex sets $A_y$ for $y \in D$, the Minkowski integral is $\int_D A_y\, d\mu(y) := A\!\left(\int_D h_{A_y}\, d\mu(y)\right)$, where $A(h)$ is the convex set with support function $h$.

nodes.name: Harmonic interpolation
nodes.statement: For a smoothly bounded domain $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ and a continuous family $\{A_\tau\}_{\tau \in \partial\Omega}$ of convex bodies, the harmonic interpolation is $A_x := \int_{\partial\Omega} A_\tau\, d\mu_x(\tau)$, where $d\mu_x$ is the harmonic measure on $\partial\Omega$ with respect to $x \in \Omega$.

nodes.name: Zonotope and zonoid
nodes.statement: A zonotope is a convex set expressible as a Minkowski sum of line segments; a zonoid is a convex set approximable in Hausdorff topology by zonotopes, equivalently a Minkowski integral of line segments.

nodes.name: Weak Brunn-Minkowski for harmonic interpolation
nodes.statement: If $A_x$ is the harmonic interpolation of $\{A_\tau\}$, then $x \mapsto \log|A_x|$ is superharmonic in $x$.
assumptions: $\{A_\tau\}_{\tau \in \partial\Omega}$ continuous family of convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^n$

nodes.name: Main Theorem: strong Brunn-Minkowski for harmonic interpolation
nodes.statement: If $A_x$ is the harmonic interpolation of $\{A_\tau\}$, then $x \mapsto |A_x|^{1/n}$ is superharmonic in $x$.
assumptions: $\{A_\tau\}_{\tau \in \partial\Omega}$ continuous family of convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^n$

nodes.name: Proof of Main Theorem (TP461.3)
nodes.statement: Approximate harmonic surface measure by atomic measures, apply classical Brunn-Minkowski to finite Minkowski sums, then pass to the limit.

nodes.name: Reduce to mean-value inequality on balls
nodes.statement: Reduce the superharmonicity to: for $B_\epsilon(x) \subseteq \Omega$, $|A_x|^{1/n} \geq \int_{\partial B_\epsilon(x)} |A_y|^{1/n}\, dS(y)$, with $dS$ the normalized Euclidean surface measure.

nodes.name: Use mean-value property of harmonic measure
nodes.statement: Use $\mu_x = \int_{\partial B_\epsilon(x)} \mu_y\, dS(y)$ to get $A_x = \int_{\partial B_\epsilon(x)} A_y\, dS(y)$.

nodes.name: Approximate by atomic measures
nodes.statement: Approximate $dS$ by atomic measures $\nu_k = \sum_{i=1}^{N_k} \lambda_{i,k} \delta_{y_{i,k}}$ with $\nu_k \to dS$ weakly; for large $k$, $\sum_i \lambda_{i,k} A_{y_{i,k}}$ is Hausdorff-close to $A_x$.

nodes.name: Apply classical Brunn-Minkowski and pass to limit
nodes.statement: $|A_x|^{1/n} + \epsilon \geq |\sum_i \lambda_{i,k} A_{y_{i,k}}|^{1/n} \geq \sum_i \lambda_{i,k} |A_{y_{i,k}}|^{1/n} \geq \int_{\partial B_\epsilon(x)} |A_y|^{1/n}\, dS(y) - \epsilon$ by classical Brunn-Minkowski; let $\epsilon \to 0$.

nodes.name: Subharmonic family of convex sets
nodes.statement: A continuous family of convex sets $A_x \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ over a domain $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ is subharmonic if whenever $B_\epsilon(x) \subseteq \Omega$, $A_x \supseteq \int_{\partial B_\epsilon(x)} A_y\, dS(y)$.

nodes.name: Subharmonic families have superharmonic volume root
nodes.statement: If $A_x$ is subharmonic over $\Omega$, then $x \mapsto |A_x|^{1/n}$ is superharmonic.
assumptions: $\{A_x\}$ subharmonic family of convex bodies over $\Omega$ (Definition DP461.7)

nodes.name: Berndtsson's theorem on slices of pseudoconvex domains
nodes.statement: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}^{n+m}$ be pseudoconvex, invariant under $y_j \mapsto y_j'$ in the first $n$ coordinates, and $U_w := \{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : (x,w) \in U\}$. Then $w \mapsto -\log|U_w|$ is plurisubharmonic in $w$.
assumptions: $U$ invariant in imaginary parts of first $n$ coordinates

nodes.name: Strengthened Berndtsson theorem (volume root version)
nodes.statement: In the same setting as Theorem TP461.4, the map $w \mapsto -|U_w|^{1/n}$ is plurisubharmonic.
assumptions: $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}^{n+m}$ pseudoconvex with imaginary-part symmetry as in TP461.4

nodes.name: Proof of strengthened Berndtsson theorem
nodes.statement: Reduce to $m=1$, show $U_w$ is a subharmonic family via support functions and Kiselman's minimum principle, then apply Corollary CP461.1.

nodes.name: Reduction and convexity setup
nodes.statement: WLOG $m = 1$; pseudoconvexity and symmetry imply $U_w$ is convex; by approximation assume bounded and continuous.

nodes.name: Recast subharmonicity via support functions
nodes.statement: Since $A \supseteq B$ iff $h_A \geq h_B$, $U_w$ is subharmonic iff $h_{U_w}(\xi) = \sup_{x \in U_w}(x \cdot \xi)$ is superharmonic in $w$ for every $\xi \in \mathbb{R}^n$.

nodes.name: Apply Kiselman's minimum principle
nodes.statement: Let $\phi$ be a plurisubharmonic exhaustion of $U$ independent of $\Im(\mathbb{C}^n)$; set $\phi_R := \max(\phi - R, 0)$ and $\psi_R(x+iy, w) := \phi_R(x+iy, w) - x \cdot \xi$. By Kiselman, $\inf_{x \in U_w} \psi_R(x,w)$ is subharmonic in $w$.

nodes.name: Take limit and conclude
nodes.statement: Since $\sup_{x \in U_w}(x \cdot \xi) = -\lim_{R \to \infty} \inf_{x \in U_w} \psi_R(x,w)$, $h_{U_w}(\xi)$ is superharmonic, so $U_w$ is subharmonic; conclude via Corollary CP461.1.

nodes.name: Characterization of harmonic case (extremal)
nodes.statement: $x \mapsto |A_x|^{1/n}$ is harmonic if and only if $A_x = c_x B + d_x$ for a fixed convex body $B \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and harmonic functions $c_x : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}_+$ and $d_x : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^n$.
assumptions: $\{A_x\}_{x \in \Omega}$ subharmonic family of convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^n$ over a domain $\Omega$
conclusions: $x \mapsto |A_x|^{1/n}$ harmonic iff $A_x = c_x B + d_x$ with $B$ fixed convex body and $c_x, d_x$ harmonic

nodes.name: Proof of extremal characterization (TP461.6)
nodes.statement: Decompose harmonic interpolation over partitions of $\partial\Omega'$, apply Brunn-Minkowski equality case, then refine partition and pass to continuous limit.

nodes.name: Reduce to harmonic interpolation on subdomain
nodes.statement: Take $\Omega' \Subset \Omega$ relatively compact with smooth boundary; subharmonicity plus harmonicity of $|A_x|^{1/n}$ forces $A_x$ to equal the harmonic interpolation of $A_y|_{\partial\Omega'}$.

nodes.name: Decompose into pieces and apply BM equality
nodes.statement: Write $\partial\Omega' = \sqcup_i D_i$, set $B_i := \int_{D_i} A_y\, d\mu_x(y)$. Then $A_x = \sum_i B_i$ and equality $|A_x|^{1/n} = \sum_i |B_i|^{1/n}$ in Brunn-Minkowski gives $B_i = c_i B + d_i$ for fixed convex $B$ (normalized: volume one, centroid at origin).

nodes.name: Refine partition and use continuity
nodes.statement: Refining $D_i$ into $E_j$ and applying continuity of $A_y$ produces continuous $c_y, d_y$ on $\partial\Omega'$ with $A_y = c_y B + d_y$; harmonic extension gives $A_x = c_x B + d_x$ on $\Omega'$.

nodes.name: Globalize
nodes.statement: Since $\Omega'$ was arbitrary, the representation $A_x = c_x B + d_x$ holds on all of $\Omega$.

nodes.name: Vitale zonoid associated to a random vector
nodes.statement: For a random vector $Y$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with finite expectation and law $\nu_v$, define the zonoid $Z(Y) := \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} [0, y]\, d\nu_v(y)$, the Minkowski integral of segments from $0$ to $y$.

nodes.name: Vitale zonoid-determinant identity
nodes.statement: $E|\det M_Y| = n!\, |Z(Y)|$, where $M_Y$ is an $(n,n)$ matrix with iid columns distributed as $Y$.
assumptions: $Y$ random vector in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with finite expectation

nodes.name: Brunn-Minkowski for expected absolute random determinants
nodes.statement: If $Y_\tau$ is a family of random vectors over $\partial\Omega$ (each with finite expectation) and $Y_x$ is defined by $\nu_{Y_x} := \int_{\partial\Omega} \nu_{Y_\tau}\, d\mu_x(\tau)$, then $x \mapsto (E|\det M_{Y_x}|)^{1/n}$ is superharmonic in $x$.
assumptions: $\{Y_\tau\}_{\tau \in \partial\Omega}$ continuous family of random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with finite expectation

nodes.name: Proof of TP461.8 via zonoids
nodes.statement: Show $Z(Y_x)$ is the harmonic interpolation of $Z(Y_\tau)$ by Fubini, then combine with Vitale identity and Theorem TP461.3.

nodes.name: Compute zonoid of interpolated law via Fubini
nodes.statement: $Z(Y_x) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} [0,y]\, d\nu_{Y_x}(y) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \int_{\partial\Omega} [0,y]\, d\mu_x(\tau)\, d\nu_{Y_\tau}(y) = \int_{\partial\Omega} Z(Y_\tau)\, d\mu_x(\tau)$, so $Z(Y_x)$ is the harmonic interpolation of $Z(Y_\tau)$.

nodes.name: Apply Vitale identity and main theorem
nodes.statement: By Vitale identity (\ref{eq:zonvol}) $E|\det M_{Y_x}| = n! |Z(Y_x)|$, so $(E|\det M_{Y_x}|)^{1/n}$ is proportional to $|Z(Y_x)|^{1/n}$, which is superharmonic by Theorem TP461.3.

nodes.name: Harmonic interpolation preserves zonoids
nodes.statement: If each boundary set $A_\tau$ is a zonoid, every member $A_x$ of the harmonic interpolating family is also a zonoid; this property fails for the convex interpolation, even when $\Omega$ is convex.
